projects.title: Master thesis
projects.subtitle: Learning code change representations via artificial intelligence code model
projects.description: My master's thesis focused on the problem of code change representation. The work presents a systematic review of existing research, a Python-based experimental framework, and a novel retrieval-augmented approach as an alternative to fine-tuning large models. The proposed methods demonstrated competitive performance while reducing computational cost.

projects.title: JakPrzyjade
projects.subtitle: Microservice-based public transit ticketing system
projects.description: A public transit ticketing system built as a set of cooperating microservices that handle user accounts, ticket purchases, and payment processing. Covers the full engineering cycle — from business modeling and requirements analysis, through architecture design, to implementation and deployment. Designed and implemented for the Software System Design university course.

projects.title: Appmedica Challenge
projects.subtitle: AI-powered email attachment summarizer
projects.description: A fullstack recruitment project implemented as a fully containerized web application. It periodically fetches emails over IMAP, summarizes their attachments with an LLM, and presents the results in a public web interface. The entire cloud infrastructure is defined as code and deployed to Google Cloud with a focus on a clean, production-ready and maintainable solution.

projects.title: jzehner.dev
projects.subtitle: The website you are looking at right now
projects.description: My personal corner of the internet — a statically prerendered portfolio built with SvelteKit and Tailwind CSS, deployed on Cloudflare Workers. All content is data-driven: profile and project entries live in JSON files validated with Zod schemas, which also generate JSON Schemas for editor autocompletion. Self-hosted fonts, semantic markup, and structured data for SEO round out the details.

projects.title: Image Steganography
projects.subtitle: Hiding messages in images, entirely in the browser
projects.description: A web application that allows users to hide messages in images using techniques such as LSB, DCT, and visual cryptography. All image processing runs client-side, powered by Rust compiled to WebAssembly. Designed and implemented for the Engineering of Security and Knowledge Acquisition from Data and Databases university course.

projects.title: ArXiv search
projects.subtitle: Full-text search over academic papers
projects.description: A web application for searching academic papers from arXiv.org, offering advanced search filters, faceted search, and user-friendly navigation on top of an Elasticsearch index. Designed and implemented for the Information Retrieval Systems university course.

projects.title: Senso
projects.subtitle: Mobile companion app for elderly people
projects.description: A group project built for my engineering thesis. A mobile application that aids the elderly in their daily life, including features such as medication reminders, emergency contacts, and an SOS button. Backed by a .NET server with a fully documented API.

projects.title: AI & Knowledge Engineering
projects.subtitle: Classic AI algorithms, written in the V language
projects.description: Projects for the Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Engineering university course, with two highlights. A route planner working on real Wrocław public transport data: shortest paths with Dijkstra and A* (using a Euclidean-distance heuristic) optimizing either travel time or the number of transfers, and shortest cycles with Tabu Search. And a Reversi engine built on Minimax with alpha-beta pruning, driven by eight heuristics — including one tuned with a genetic algorithm.

projects.title: Advent of Code 2022
projects.subtitle: Every day in a different programming language
projects.description: My solutions to Advent of Code 2022, with a self-imposed twist: every day had to be solved in a language not used on any previous day. Seventeen days, seventeen languages — from Rust, TypeScript and F# through OCaml, Julia and Crystal to Gleam, ReasonML and V — with both puzzle parts completed each day. A fun exercise in picking up new syntax, tooling, and paradigms quickly.
